SERIES: 'WHO - ERITREA Weekly Epidemiological Bulletin' (WHO Eritrea country office), 2009, 16 issues (weeks 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, 22, 23, 34, 40, 42, 43, 44) listed on the archived AFRO page www.afro.who.int/eritrea/eritrea-publications/bulletins.html (Wayback 2011-01-29) as docman gid 4894-4909, all retrieved from the Wayback Machine as PDFs. Never registered or read by any prior ERI agent (metadata grep 'weekly epidemiological bulletin' = 0). Each issue prints a zoba table 'Reported cases and deaths of the epidemic prone disease' (Table 2 in weeks 5-12 'as of week N', Table 3 'on week N' from week 13) with C/D columns for Anseba, Debub, Gash Barka, Maekel, NRS, SRS and Total (cases only from week 42) and an explicit Cholera row; 'Note: C =Cases: D=Deaths, NA=Not Available'. The text states which zobas submitted that week and Table 1 gives reporting timeliness/completeness for 250-251 health facilities (completeness 92-97 percent). ACCEPTANCE RULE applied by Agent 2 because the instrument has two demonstrated defects: (i) week 11 prints Gash-Barka as 0 for EVERY disease (malaria 0, bloody diarrhoea 0) although the text says 'the Gash Barka Region submitted reports up to week 10' - a non-report printed as 0; (ii) the week-12 Anseba, Debub and SRS columns are identical to week 11 (malaria 3/30/0, bloody diarrhoea 81/110/2) - a suspected carry-over. A zoba-week cholera zero is therefore accepted ONLY if the cholera cell is 0 (not NA), the text does not say that zoba failed to report that week, and the same column carries a non-zero count of another disease that week (malaria or bloody diarrhoea), proving a genuine report; a national zero is written only for weeks in which all six zobas pass (weeks 13, 19, 22, 23, 43). Result: 80 zoba-week Documented_Absence rows and 5 national rows; rejected: every NA cell, Gash-Barka week 11, and Anseba/Debub/SRS week 12. CONTEXT: these are the first observations of any kind for Eritrea inside effective gap G4 (2009-01-01..2010-12-31); WER 85(31) says 'Eight African countries reported 0 cases' in 2009 without naming them (metadata 105). The same series reports positives when they exist (bloody diarrhoea 187-774 cases a week; a measles outbreak in Debub Denkalia sub-zone, SRS, Feb 2009), so the cholera zeros are an operating line of a functioning IDSR report, not a template default.

Description: Verbatim (Nationen 20 Sep 1977 p.14, 'Kolera-frammarsj i Midt-Østen', dateline 'Damaskus (NTB-Reuter-UPI)'): 'I en leir for etiopiske krigsfanger i Eritrea-provinsen har fem soldater mistet livet etter symptomer på kolera-angrep, og flere hundre fanger er kommet i faresonen på grunn av de dårlige sanitære forholdene. It is difficult to bring medicines into the area.' The report is datelined Damascus on Monday 19 Sep 1977 inside a round-up of the 1977 Middle East El Tor epidemic (Syria 3,100+ cases); a Damascus origin points to a liberation-front statement - the ELF kept an office there and both fronts then held several thousand Ethiopian prisoners - but the wire does not name the source, the camp or the zone. FIRST EVIDENCE OF ANY KIND FOR ERITREAN CHOLERA IN 1977 apart from metadata 194, and the first in the 1975-1984 interval. Level 3 (major news agencies), single origin, clinical description only ('symptoms of a cholera attack'), not laboratory-confirmed, uncorroborated by WHO (Ethiopia notified no cholera in 1977).
